title: Bounded-above flat replacement on a ringed site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and $N$ an integer. Every cochain complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with $\mathcal F^i=0$ for $i>N$ admits a bounded-above complex $\mathcal E^\bullet$ of flat $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], with $\mathcal E^i=0$ for $i>N$, and a termwise surjective quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] $\mathcal E^\bullet\to\mathcal F^\bullet$. These replacements can be chosen functorially for maps of bounded-above complexes.

source.place: Lemma 06YS (bounded-above flat replacement used in its proof)

proof.text: Choose T and pi using [lem-pc-sites-modules-functorial-flat-cover]. Zero module sheaves are flat: install the additive symmetric monoidal structure from [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], and apply the proved source lemma ObjectProperty.flat_of_isZero, taking its right tensor exactness clause. Apply [lem-pc-functorial-cycle-pullback-construction] with S=SheafOfModules.IsFlat to obtain Q, epsilon, flat terms, the same bound, and the compatible-pair lifting property.

To prove epsilon^i epic, use Mathlib epi_iff_surjective_up_to_refinements. Given y:B to F^i, first apply the compatible-pair property in degree i+1 to (0,d_F y). This gives, after an epic refinement p1, a cycle x1 lifting d_F y. Apply the property in degree i to (x1,p1 y). The resulting x2 lifts p2 p1 y, and the composite refinement is epic. This proves termwise epimorphy.

For each degree i use quasiIsoAt_iff_isIso_homologyMap and isIso_iff_mono_and_epi. Mathlib HomologicalComplex.mono_homologyMap_iff_up_to_refinements reduces monicity to lifting a cycle x whose image is a boundary d_F y. The compatible-pair property in degree i-1 gives z with d_E z=p x, exactly the required local boundary lift. HomologicalComplex.epi_homologyMap_iff_up_to_refinements reduces epimorphy to lifting a target cycle y. Apply the compatible-pair property in degree i to (0,y): the resulting z is a cycle and its image is p y, so take the correction boundary to be zero. Thus each homology map is an isomorphism and epsilon is a quasi-isomorphism.

lean.statement: theorem exists_functorial_boundedAbove_flat_replacement {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (N : ℤ) : let A := SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R) let P : ObjectProperty (CochainComplex A ℤ) := fun F => ∀ (i : ℤ), N < i → IsZero (F.X i) ∃ Q : P.FullSubcategory ⥤ CochainComplex A ℤ, ∃ ε : Q ⟶ P.ι, ∀ F : P.FullSubcategory, (∀ (i : ℤ), SheafOfModules.IsFlat ((Q.obj F).X i)) ∧ (∀ (i : ℤ), N < i → IsZero ((Q.obj F).X i)) ∧ (∀ (i : ℤ), Epi ((ε.app F).f i)) ∧ QuasiIso (ε.app F)
